mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in unemployment benefits (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the labor participation rate (UNRATE) creates a dual signal of weak demand and reduced labor supply, pushing S&P 500 20-day forward returns negative.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >5% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2% in the same month
failure_condition: Over 50% of triggered periods show non-significant negative returns (p > 0.05) or returns opposite to the predicted direction.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in consumer confidence (not directly observable in the provided proxies) proxies demand momentum that precedes S&P 500 gains within 5 trading days, assuming demand proxies like HOUST show early acceleration.
failure_condition: Rank IC of HOUST vs. SPX forward returns < 0.05 over 5-day windows, or 20-day returns are not statistically higher than baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 index for two consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness that lags into S&P 500 declines over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100 and remains below for two months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than the prior 20-day window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +2% in a month, it signals accelerating inflation expectations that compress equity discount rates and drive negative 20-day forward S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Over 40% of such events produce non-negative 20-day returns (p > 0.6), or IC < -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months suggests labor market tightening that raises the cost of capital and suppresses S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% and remains below for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 60-day period (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both retail sales (not directly observable) and industrial production (INDPRO) above 100 index implies robust demand that is associated with positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: More than 40% of high INDPRO periods fail to produce positive 20-day forward returns (p > 0.6).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip in supply indicators—first a sharp drop in RSAFS followed by a recovery—creates uncertainty that precedes S&P 500 volatility spikes and negative 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls by >10% in a month then recovers by >5% in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day returns during such episodes are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) or volatility is not elevated compared to baseline.
